text: Praise the LORD! Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise in the assembly of the faithful.
Let Israel rejoice in his Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King.

versions.text: Let Israel rejoice in their Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King.
versions.explanation: Israel is a singular collective in Hebrew (יִשְׂמַח, singular verb, with singular suffix on בְּעֹשָׂיו). 'their Maker' creates a number mismatch with the singular subject; 'his Maker' is more consistent, though a fully plural rendering ('Let the people of Israel rejoice in their Maker') would also work.

text: Let them praise his name with dancing, making music to him with tambourine and lyre.
For the LORD delights in his people; he crowns the humble with salvation.
Let the faithful exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds.
Let the exaltation of God be in their mouths and a two-edged sword in their hands,

versions.text: Let the high praises of God be in their throats and a two-edged sword in their hands,
versions.explanation: 'High praises ... in their throats' is a literal echo that reads awkwardly aloud; 'in their mouths' conveys the sense of the throat as the organ of song more naturally for oral reading.

text: to execute vengeance on the nations and punishment on the peoples,
to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron,
to carry out against them the judgment that is written. This is honor for all his faithful ones. Praise the LORD!

versions.text: to carry out the judgment written against them. This is glory for all his faithful ones. Praise the LORD!
versions.explanation: The Hebrew הָדָר denotes honor or splendor rather than כָּבוֹד 'glory' used in verse 5; distinguishing the two avoids blurring the vocabulary. Reordering also lets the phrase read more naturally aloud.
